article.title: Why More Features Can Make a Customer Model Worse
article.why: Balance predictive information with leakage, stability, and production cost.

paragraphs.en:
When a team has hundreds of customer variables, it is tempting to put all of them into a machine-learning model. More information seems as if it should produce better predictions. Sometimes it does, but more features can also make a model worse, especially when the goal is reliable production performance rather than a strong score on one historical test set.

The first danger is leakage. A variable may contain information that would not actually be available at prediction time. For example, a field updated after a customer purchases insurance may strongly predict that purchase. The model can achieve excellent validation performance while learning information from the future. When deployed before purchase, the feature is unavailable or misleading, and performance collapses.

A second problem is instability. Some behavioral variables are useful in one period because of a temporary campaign, system change, or unusual event. A model can rely heavily on these signals and then fail when the environment changes. Comparing feature distributions and importance across time helps identify variables whose relationship with the target is fragile.

Redundancy also matters. Ten highly correlated versions of the same spending measure may add little new information. Tree models can often handle correlated inputs, but excessive duplication makes interpretation harder and may cause importance to be distributed unpredictably among similar variables. It also increases the work required to define, test, and maintain the feature pipeline.

Missingness creates another operational risk. A feature may look powerful in training data but depend on a source system that is delayed or incomplete in production. If the missing-data pattern changes, predictions can shift. Teams should therefore evaluate not only statistical importance but also availability, freshness, definition stability, and fallback behavior.

There is also a governance cost. Every feature has lineage: where it comes from, when it is calculated, what business definition it uses, and who owns it. A model with 500 poorly documented variables may be harder to reproduce and audit than a model with 100 well-understood variables, even if their offline accuracy is similar. Simpler models can sometimes be more valuable because they are easier to monitor and repair.

A practical feature-selection process therefore asks several questions. Does the feature improve out-of-time performance? Is it available before the decision? Is its definition stable? Does it add information beyond existing variables? Can the production pipeline calculate it reliably and on time? Is the improvement large enough to justify the operational complexity?

Feature selection is not simply about making the model smaller. It is about selecting information that will still be trustworthy when the model is used. The best feature set is not necessarily the largest one. It is the set that provides enough predictive signal while remaining temporally valid, operationally reliable, interpretable, and maintainable.
paragraphs.zh:
當團隊有數百個顧客變數時，很容易認為全部放進模型就會更準。但若目標是 production 的可靠表現，而不是某一次歷史 test set 的高分，更多 feature 也可能讓模型更差。

第一個風險是 leakage。某欄位可能包含 prediction time 根本不會有的資訊，例如保險購買後才更新的欄位，會讓 validation 看似極佳，但部署到購買前就失效。

第二是 instability。某些行為變數只因暫時 campaign、系統變更或特殊事件而有效；環境改變後關係可能消失。應比較不同時間的 feature distribution 與 importance。

Redundancy 也會增加問題。十個高度相關的消費額版本未必增加多少新資訊，卻使解釋、pipeline 定義與維護更複雜。Missingness 同樣重要：training 中強大的 feature 若 production source 延遲或缺漏，預測就可能漂移。因此除了 statistical importance，也要評估 availability、freshness、definition stability 與 fallback。

每個 feature 還有 governance cost：來源、計算時間、business definition、owner 都要能追蹤。500個文件不足的變數，可能比100個清楚定義的變數更難重現、audit 與維護。

實務 feature selection 應問：是否改善 out-of-time performance？決策前是否可取得？定義是否穩定？是否提供既有變數之外的新資訊？production 能否準時可靠計算？改善幅度是否值得增加 operational complexity？

因此 feature selection 不是單純把模型縮小，而是選擇部署後仍可信的資訊。最佳 feature set 不一定最大，而是 predictive signal、時間有效性、可靠性、可解釋性與維護性之間的平衡。
paragraphs.ja:
顧客変数が数百あると、全部modelに入れれば精度が上がるように思えます。しかしproductionで安定して使うことが目的なら、featureを増やすほど悪化する場合もあります。

第一のriskはleakageです。購入後に更新される項目など、prediction timeには存在しない情報を使えばvalidationは高くても本番では再現できません。

第二はinstabilityです。一時的なcampaign、system変更、特殊イベントのために効いていた行動変数は、環境が変わると関係が消える可能性があります。期間別にdistributionやimportanceを比較する必要があります。

redundancyも問題です。似た利用額指標を大量に入れても新しい情報は少なく、解釈とpipeline maintenanceが複雑になります。missingnessも重要で、trainingでは取得できてもproduction sourceが遅延すれば予測が変化します。importanceだけでなくavailability、freshness、definition stability、fallbackを確認します。

さらに各featureにはlineageとgovernance costがあります。どこから来て、いつ計算され、どの定義で、誰がownerかを管理する必要があります。500個の不明確な変数より100個の理解された変数のほうが再現・audit・repairしやすい場合があります。

実務ではout-of-time performanceを改善するか、decision前に利用可能か、定義が安定しているか、既存feature以上の情報を持つか、本番で期限内に計算できるか、複雑性に見合う改善かを確認します。最良のfeature setは最大のsetではなく、本番でも信頼できるsetです。

vocabulary.usage: Check for target or temporal leakage.
The relationship may be fragile over time.
The model should be easy to audit.
The feature must be temporally valid.
Define fallback behavior for missing sources.

business.term: Offline importance is not enough; the feature must be available and stable at decision time.
business.explanation: 強調 production feature 的必要條件。

sources: Machine-learning feature leakage, temporal validation, data lineage, and production monitoring practices.
